I have been farming these 18 mu in Quzhou for ten years. My family has four people, and between my husband, my mother-in-law, and me, we have enough hands for the busy seasons. We need grain to eat and cash for the children's school fees, so I keep the biggest plot in wheat-maize rotation and use the smaller plots for vegetables and that stevia contract with the processing company.

This year, the 12 mu for wheat and maize is my foundation. I will sow wheat right after we harvest maize in early October — improved seed from the township station, not traditional seed, because the new varieties resist rust better and the grain buyers pay more for clean, uniform grain. I will rotary-till the field after clearing the maize stubble. I will spread compound fertilizer as base dressing and top-dress urea at green-up and jointing — about 15 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, plus phosphorus and potassium from the compound bag. I will irrigate four times: winter water if the sky stays dry, then jointing, heading, and grain-filling water. Two pesticide sprays will do, one for weeds at seedling stage and one for aphids. If frost does not come early, I expect around 500 kg per mu.

Maize goes into that same 12 mu the day after wheat harvest in early June. There is no time to plough — I will use no-tillage planting straight into the wheat stubble. I only buy hybrid seed; I learned years ago that hybrid maize pays for itself even though the seed is expensive. I will apply similar fertilizer to wheat, maybe a little less nitrogen, around 14 kg per mu. Three irrigations: one at jointing/tasseling, one at filling, and one more if August turns hot. Two sprays — herbicide at planting, and insecticide when the corn borers show up. I should get 600 kg per mu.

For the vegetables, I keep 3 mu for autumn cabbage on the east plot. I will sow hybrid F1 seeds in July. Cabbage is greedy — I will put down plenty of chicken manure and about 20 kg nitrogen equivalent per mu in chemical fertilizer. Five irrigations, because the heads crack if they go dry. Four pesticide sprays; the diamondback moths never sleep in autumn. I hope for 4000 kg per mu.

Eggplant gets 2 mu. I will start seedlings in the courtyard in March and transplant after the last frost. Hybrid seeds again. Eggplant needs water steady, so five irrigations, and I will spray four times for the fruit borer and red spider mite. Yield should be around 3000 kg per mu if the market price does not crash.

Stevia is only 1 mu, but the company pays a fixed price, so it is safe money. I will use improved seedlings they provide. It needs less nitrogen than the vegetables, about 10 kg per mu, but more potassium. Four irrigations, two pesticide sprays. Dried leaf should be 200 kg per mu.

My well has enough water for all of this if I irrigate at night and rotate between plots.
